text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success, and the SMART framework is a powerful tool to guide this process. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase user engagement by 20% within six months." Once your goals are defined, you break the project into smaller milestones – key checkpoints that mark progress. Each milestone should have its own deliverables, which are the tangible outputs, like reports or prototypes. Finally, it is crucial to achieve stakeholder alignment early on. This means ensuring everyone involved, from team members to clients, agrees on the goals and the path forward, preventing misunderstandings later.
